title: Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports: what do they show, who sees names and what do they cost?
summary: The reporting behaviour, privacy control, role assignments and API calls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The two Copilot report routes omit a section heading but otherwise lead to the right reports.

claims.where: summary
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center usage dashboards show how people use Microsoft 365 services, including Copilot.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports provide insight into how people in your organization use Microsoft 365 for business services.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Microsoft says the reports show who uses a service most and who barely uses it and might not need a Microsoft 365 license.
claims.quote: you can see who uses a service to the fullest extent and who barely uses it and might not need a Microsoft 365 license.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: Reports > Usage > View more on a service card opens the service's report tabs.
claims.quote: Select View more from the at-a-glance activity card for a service (such as email or OneDrive) to see the report details page. On that page, different reports for the service are provided in tabs.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: Usage reports generally cover the last 7, 30, 90 and 180 days.
claims.quote: Usage reports are generally available for the last 7, 30, 90, and 180 days.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: Reports typically become available within 24 to 72 hours but sometimes take several days.
claims.quote: The reports typically become available within 24 to 72 hours, but might sometimes take several days to become available.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report offers the last 7, 28, 90 or 180 days.
claims.quote: You can view the Microsoft Copilot report over the last 7, 28, 90, or 180 days.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report offers the last 7 or 30 days.
claims.quote: You can view the Copilot Credits report over the last 7 or 30 days.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report is at Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Copilot > Usage.
claims.quote: On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Copilot. ... On the report page, select the Usage tab to view adoption and usage metrics.
claims.fix: Include the Reports heading on the Usage page: 'Reports > Usage > Reports > Microsoft Copilot > Copilot > Usage'. The cited page says 'under Reports'; the existing route otherwise gives the correct choices.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report is at Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Credits.
claims.quote: On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Credits.
claims.fix: Include the Reports heading on the Usage page: 'Reports > Usage > Reports > Microsoft Copilot > Credits'. The cited page says 'under Reports'; the existing route otherwise gives the correct choices.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: Microsoft's reporting-options article instead describes selecting Microsoft Copilot > Usage after Reports > Usage.
claims.quote: To view reports, go to Reports > Usage. ... Select Microsoft Copilot > Readiness or Usage:

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report shows enabled users, defined as users with Microsoft Copilot licences over the selected timeframe.
claims.quote: Enabled Users shows the total number of unique users in your organization with Microsoft Copilot licenses over the selected timeframe.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report shows active users.
claims.quote: Active Users shows the total number of enabled users in your organization who tried a user-initiated Microsoft Copilot feature, in one or more apps in Microsoft 365 over the selected timeframe.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot usage report shows prompts submitted.
claims.quote: Total prompts submitted shows the total number of prompts users sent to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the selected time frame.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report shows credits used per user.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report shows credits used per agent.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report shows credits used per billing policy.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report shows credits used per agent-user pair.
claims.quote: Credits used per user, per agent, per billing policy, and per agent-user pair

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report covers Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies.
claims.quote: This report gives you visibility into credits used for your Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies.

claims.where: What it is: How they work
claims.claim: By default all usage reports hide usernames, display names, groups and sites.
claims.quote: By default, all reports hide user information such as usernames, display names, groups, and sites to help companies support local privacy laws.

claims.where: summary
claims.claim: One organisation-level setting hides or shows identifying user, group and site information in usage reports.
claims.quote: The organization setting that hides or shows this information applies to the following properties:

claims.where: What it is: Other Copilot reporting sources
claims.claim: Microsoft lists the Microsoft 365 admin center as one of four main sources of Copilot reports.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot offers four main sources for usage reports. ... Microsoft 365 admin center: Provides readiness and usage reports focused on license eligibility, adoption, and basic usage metrics.

claims.where: What it is: Other Copilot reporting sources
claims.claim: Viva Insights Copilot Analytics, including the Copilot Dashboard, is another of those four sources.
claims.quote: Viva Insights Copilot Analytics: Offers comprehensive Copilot analytics through the Copilot Dashboard and Advanced Insights Analyst workbench for detailed metrics and custom reporting.

claims.where: What it is: Other Copilot reporting sources
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview audit logs are another of Microsoft's four Copilot reporting sources.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview audit logs: Delivers detailed audit logs of all Copilot activities for compliance tracking and security auditing.

claims.where: What it is: Other Copilot reporting sources
claims.claim: Power Platform and Copilot Studio analytics are another of Microsoft's four Copilot reporting sources.
claims.quote: Power Platform & Copilot Studio Analytics: Provides consumption metrics for Copilot agents and detailed analytics on agent performance.

claims.where: What it is: Other Copilot reporting sources
claims.claim: Viva Feature Access Management governs the Copilot Dashboard through the Viva Insights web app control.
claims.quote: Turning this control off disables the entire app, which includes the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, Copilot Analytics reports, and advanced analysis and admin tools.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Copilot adoption reporting shows which Microsoft 365 apps people use with Copilot.
claims.quote: In the Adoption section, Adoption by app shows enabled users and active users of Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: The Credits report makes metered consumption visible for users without a Microsoft Copilot licence who interact with agents in Copilot Chat that spin the Copilot Studio meter.
claims.quote: The Credits used metric shows the total credits used from interactions by users in your organization who don't have a Microsoft Copilot license and are interacting with agents in Copilot Chat that spin the Copilot Studio meter during the selected time period.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Global Administrators can change the organisation setting to reveal concealed information.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: The conceal setting also applies to Microsoft Graph usage reports.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: The conceal setting also applies to Power BI usage reports.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: The conceal setting also applies to Teams admin center usage reports.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Concealment also anonymises identifying information in report exports.
claims.quote: The Global administrator can hide identifiable information (using MD5 hashes) such as display name, group name, email, and Microsoft Entra user ID in the report and its export.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The usage reports overview lists viewing roles but names no separate viewing licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports viewing separate license charge pricing. Read the usage reports overview in full, including Before you begin and View licensing information; no separate viewing licence is named there.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The usage reports overview names no separate viewing charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports viewing separate license charge pricing. Read the usage reports overview in full and search excerpts about admin-center reports; the overview names no separate viewing charge.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Usage reports do not include perpetual license models.
claims.quote: Usage reports don't include perpetual license models.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Names are hidden by default
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report's Billing Policy ID and user names are governed by the same hidden-data setting.
claims.quote: By default, the Copilot credits report anonymizes the Billing Policy ID, just like the username and display name. ... Changes to this hidden data setting affect the username, display name, and Billing Policy ID.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The setting is a logged event
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview records usage-report privacy-setting changes as UpdateUsageReportsPrivacySetting, with friendly name Updated usage report privacy settings.
claims.quote: Updated usage report privacy settings | UpdateUsageReportsPrivacySetting | Admin updated privacy settings for usage reports.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Role choice decides what a reader sees
claims.claim: Usage Summary Reports Reader can view usage reports without user details.
claims.quote: Usage Summary Reports Reader (with no user details).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Role choice decides what a reader sees
claims.claim: User Experience Success Manager can view usage reports without user details.
claims.quote: User Experience Success Manager (with no user details)

claims.where: Risks and limits: Role choice decides what a reader sees
claims.claim: Global Reader gets tenant-level data only in the Microsoft Graph reports API.
claims.quote: The Global Reader and Usage Summary Reports Reader roles will only have access to tenant-level data, without visibility into detailed metrics.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Role choice decides what a reader sees
claims.claim: Usage Summary Reports Reader gets tenant-level data only in the Microsoft Graph reports API.
claims.quote: The Global Reader and Usage Summary Reports Reader roles will only have access to tenant-level data, without visibility into detailed metrics.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Data lags
claims.claim: Copilot activity typically becomes available within about 48 hours.
claims.quote: For Copilot activity on a given day, the report typically becomes available within 48 hours of the end of that day (in UTC).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Data lags
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report must be refreshed manually to show recent usage.
claims.quote: The report shows data up to today, but it doesn't automatically update if there's recent usage. To view the latest data, manually refresh the report.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot Credits report history is short
claims.claim: During preview the Copilot Credits report displays at most 30 days of history.
claims.quote: During preview, the report displays a maximum of 30 days of Copilot Credits history.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot Credits report history is short
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report does not provide usage information from before 3 May 2025.
claims.quote: In addition, usage information from before May 3, 2025, isn't available in the report.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Alerts are report cards, not limits
claims.claim: The Credits report shows an Alerts card when a user consumes more than 3,000 credits in the past 30 days.
claims.quote: The Alerts card is visible in the report when one or more users consume more than 3,000 credits in the past 30 days.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Alerts are report cards, not limits
claims.claim: A similar Credits report alert appears for users consuming 2,000 to 3,000 credits.
claims.quote: If users consume 2,000 to 3,000 credits, a similar alert appears.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Alerts are report cards, not limits
claims.claim: The Credits report alerts are report cards rather than spending limits.
claims.quote: The Alerts card is visible in the report when one or more users consume more than 3,000 credits in the past 30 days. ... Select View Copilot credits details to see the user list and export it to CSV.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Not every cloud has every report
claims.claim: The usage reports overview lists the Copilot Credits report as available only in the public cloud.
claims.quote: Report | Public | GCC | GCC-High | DoD | Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet ... Microsoft Copilot credits | Yes | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A

claims.where: Risks and limits: Not every cloud has every report
claims.claim: Other reports are listed as not yet released in some clouds.
claims.quote: Microsoft browser usage | Yes | N/A^1^ | N/A^1^ | N/A^1^ | N/A^1^ ... N/A^1^: The report will be released in the future.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No per-user lookup
claims.claim: The usage reports cannot generate a cross-service usage list by entering a user's account.
claims.quote: You can't generate a report where you enter a user's account and then get a list of which services they're using and how much.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No per-user lookup
claims.claim: Administrators can research a specific user's usage by sorting a service report or exporting it.
claims.quote: open the Mailbox usage report, and sort the users by name. If you have thousands of users, export the report to Excel, Power BI, or use the Microsoft Graph reports API.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted users disappear
claims.claim: Microsoft deletes a deleted user's usage data within 30 days.
claims.quote: When you delete a user account, Microsoft deletes that user's usage data within 30 days.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted users disappear
claims.claim: Usage chart totals continue to include deleted users for periods when they were active.
claims.quote: The usage chart totals still include deleted users for the periods they were active, but they don't appear in the User Details table.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot usage by Graph excludes unlicensed users
claims.claim: The Copilot usage API returns usage data only for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: This API only returns usage data for users who have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Unlicensed Copilot Chat usage data isn't available through Microsoft Graph reports APIs.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The conceal control is in Microsoft 365 admin center at Settings > Org Settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/admin/reportSettings changes tenant-level report settings.
claims.quote: Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports. ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings

claims.where: controls[0].note
claims.claim: The report settings request body sets displayConcealedNames, with true concealing identifying information.
claims.quote: displayConcealedNames | Boolean | If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: Assign a reporting role in Microsoft Entra admin center through Identity > Users > All users > user > Assigned roles > Add assignment > role.
claims.quote: Expand the Identity menu > Users > select All users. ... Select the user. ... Choose Assigned roles, and then Add assignment. ... Select the appropriate role, and click Add.

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates the Microsoft Entra role assignment controlling the user's reporting access.
claims.quote: Create a role assignment for the directory provider: ... POST /roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role the Graph reference names for creating a directory role assignment.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation. Privileged Role Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: The role assignment request body identifies the reporting role through roleDefinitionId.
claims.quote: Note the use of the roleTemplateId for roleDefinitionId. roleDefinitionId can be either the service-wide template Id or the directory-specific roleDefinitionId.

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: The role assignment request body identifies the user through principalId.
claims.quote: principalId | String | Required. Identifier of the principal to which the assignment is granted.

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: directoryScopeId set to / gives the directory role assignment tenant-wide scope.
claims.quote: For the directory (Microsoft Entra ID) provider, this property supports the following formats: - / for tenant-wide scope

claims.where: Governance controls: Conceal setting notes
claims.claim: The Teams reporting reference labels the same organisation setting Display concealed user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: choose to Display concealed user, group, and site names in all reports. This setting gets applied both to the usage reports in Microsoft 365 admin center as well as Teams admin center.

claims.where: Governance controls: API reader
claims.claim: Reading the Copilot usage report API requires Reports.Read.All permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | Reports.Read.All | Not available. ... Application | Reports.Read.All | Not available.

claims.where: Governance controls: API reader
claims.claim: Delegated usage-report API calls also require the signed-in user to hold an appropriate limited administrator role.
claims.quote: In addition to the app having been granted the required permissions, the user must be a member of a Microsoft Entra ID limited administrator role.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot usage API call
claims.claim: GET /v1.0/copilot/reports/getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetail(period='D7') reads the Copilot usage report.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/reports/getMicrosoft365CopilotUsageUserDetail(period='D7')

claims.where: Governance controls: Report settings permission
claims.claim: ReportSettings.ReadWrite.All is the Graph permission for changing report settings.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | ReportSettings.ReadWrite.All | Not available. ... Application | ReportSettings.ReadWrite.All | Not available.
